dialogue.content: 本日はよろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you for seeing me today.

dialogue.content: こちらこそよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: The pleasure is all mine. Thank you for coming.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。本日はいかがされましたか？
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm your counselor. What brings you in today?

dialogue.content: こんにちは
dialogue.English: Hello.

dialogue.content: 最近、何に対してもやる気がおきなくて、、、、
dialogue.English: Lately, I just don't have the motivation to do anything...

dialogue.content: 自分でもどうしちゃったんだろうって思ってるんです。
dialogue.English: I've been wondering what's wrong with me.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。気持ちが沈む時はありますものね。
dialogue.English: I see. It's natural to feel down sometimes.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 何もする気が起きないんです
dialogue.English: I don't feel like doing anything at all.

dialogue.content: 突然、何事にもやる気が起きてこなくなったのですか？
dialogue.English: Did this lack of motivation for everything come on suddenly?

dialogue.content: 最近、会社を辞めて、それからやる気がなくなりました
dialogue.English: I quit my job recently, and since then, I've lost all motivation.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。会社を辞められたのは、どうしてですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Why did you decide to leave your company?

dialogue.content: 人間関係トラブルと自分のやりたい仕事ができなくて辞めました。
dialogue.English: I quit because of issues with my coworkers and because I couldn't do the work I wanted to do.

dialogue.content: 色々と困難が重なったのですね。人間関係は複雑で難しいですものね。以前はやりたい仕事はできていたのですか？
dialogue.English: It sounds like you were facing several difficulties at once. Human relationships can be complex and challenging. Were you able to do the work you wanted to do before?

dialogue.content: いえ、いろいろ模索中でした。
dialogue.English: No, I was still exploring various options.

dialogue.content: それで転職して、やっと自分のやりたい仕事を見つけれたところだったのですが、
dialogue.English: So I changed jobs, and I had finally found the work I wanted to do, but...

dialogue.content: 先輩がさせてくれなくて
dialogue.English: My senior colleague wouldn't let me do it.

dialogue.content: それでも、勉強は続けてがんばってたのですが、もうここで働くのは無理だなと思い辞めました
dialogue.English: Still, I kept studying and trying my best, but I realized I couldn't continue working there, so I quit.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。ようやく見つかったご自身の転機を潰されてしまうのは、すごく辛いですね。
dialogue.English: I understand. It must be incredibly painful to have such an important opportunity crushed after you'd finally found it.

dialogue.content: そうですね、、、、
dialogue.English: Yes, it is...

dialogue.content: その先輩とは、以前からあまり上手く付き合いができていなかったのですか？
dialogue.English: Did you have a difficult relationship with that senior colleague from the start?

dialogue.content: 入社した当初は普通だったのですが、
dialogue.English: It was normal when I first joined the company, but...

dialogue.content: プライベートな話をするときは特に問題ないのですが、仕事のことになると
dialogue.English: There were no problems when we talked about personal things, but when it came to work...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: 何も教えてくれませんね
dialogue.English: They wouldn't teach me anything.

dialogue.content: 違う部署の先輩に相談すると、それはパワハラだよって。よく分からないタイミングで叱責されたり、先輩なのに適切に指導されないなど、、、、。
dialogue.English: When I consulted a senior from another department, they told me it was power harassment. For example, I'd be reprimanded at inexplicable times, and despite them being my senior, I wasn't receiving proper guidance, and so on.

dialogue.content: なので、ここではあなたのやりたいことは出来ないから、辞めて違うところで働くべきと言われたので、辞めることにしました
dialogue.English: So, they told me I wouldn't be able to do what I wanted there and that I should quit and work somewhere else, so I decided to leave.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's what happened.

dialogue.content: はき
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 辞めてスッキリ気持ちを切り替えたいのですが、なんだかもやもやが残っていて、どうも落ち着きません
dialogue.English: I want to quit and make a fresh start, but I have this lingering feeling of unease and just can't seem to settle down.

dialogue.content: どうしてそのようなことをされるのか分からず、パワハラをされるのは、凄く耐え難いくしんどいですよね。
dialogue.English: It's incredibly difficult and painful to endure power harassment without understanding why it's happening to you.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。辞められた後、元々決まっていた転職先に就職することはできていますか？
dialogue.English: I see. After you quit, were you able to start at the new job you had lined up?

dialogue.content: 怒る理由を話してくれれば、意味がわかるのですが、明らかに自分の思い通りにならなかったから、私に当たってるんだなぁというのがわかりました。
dialogue.English: If they had told me why they were angry, I might have understood, but it became clear they were just taking it out on me because things weren't going their way.

dialogue.content: 最近辞めたばかりなので、まだ就活中です。
dialogue.English: I just quit recently, so I'm still job hunting.

dialogue.content: 感情的な先輩だったのですね。訳も分からず当たられるのは精神的に辛いですよね。
dialogue.English: So they were an emotional person. Being lashed out at for no apparent reason must be mentally exhausting.

dialogue.content: はい、、、、疲れましたね
dialogue.English: Yes... It was exhausting.

dialogue.content: 決まっていた転職先に就職が叶わなかったのですね。ただでさえ辛いのに、辛いことが追い打ちのように重なったのですね。
dialogue.English: So you weren't able to get the job you had planned for. That must feel like one painful thing piling on top of another.

dialogue.content: あ。まだ転職先は決まってません。
dialogue.English: Oh. I don't have a new job lined up yet.

dialogue.content: これから再度、転職活動を行われるのですね。
dialogue.English: So you're going to start your job search again now.

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: やりたい仕事ができてたら、まだよかったのかもしれませんね
dialogue.English: If I’d been able to do the work I wanted, maybe it would have been better.

dialogue.content: 今は気が抜けたのか？ストレスなのか？わからないですが、何にもやる気がおきません
dialogue.English: Now, I don't know if it's because I'm burnt out or stressed, but I have no motivation for anything.

dialogue.content: ごはんもおいしくありません。
dialogue.English: Even food doesn't taste good.

dialogue.content: それはやるせないですよね。すごく辛いですよね。
dialogue.English: That must be so disheartening. It sounds incredibly painful.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 折角見つかった自分のやりたい仕事を邪魔された挙句、嫌がらせ・パワハラを受けて、
dialogue.English: After finally finding the kind of work you wanted, you were obstructed and subjected to harassment and power harassment, and...

dialogue.content: やっと今の仕事をやめれたけども自分のやりたかった仕事、就職先に行くことができなかったとなると、
dialogue.English: and then finally leaving that job but not being able to move on to the work or position you wanted...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 自分はこれまで何をしてきたのか、何がしたかったのか、訳が分からなくなりますね。
dialogue.English: It can make you feel lost, wondering what you've been doing all this time and what you even wanted in the first place.

dialogue.content: 本当に大変でしたね。
dialogue.English: You've really been through a lot.

dialogue.content: そうですね、、、。ずーっと、やりたくない仕事をしてきて、しんどい思いをしてきました。それで、やっと出会えた仕事でした。
dialogue.English: I think so... I've been doing work I didn't want to do for so long, and it's been hard. And then, I finally found a job I was excited about.

dialogue.content: 期待もありましたね。
dialogue.English: I had high hopes.

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.content: まだ新人だから、出来ることは少ないかもしれないけど、
dialogue.English: I knew I was new and there might not be much I could do, but...

dialogue.content: 少しでも経験を積んでいこうと決心して飛び込んでみたのですが、、、、
dialogue.English: I was determined to gain as much experience as I could, so I jumped in, but...

dialogue.content: やっぱりダメでした。
dialogue.English: It didn't work out after all.

dialogue.content: 自分のことを見失いかけてるのかも
dialogue.English: Maybe I'm starting to lose sight of myself.

dialogue.content: 何をすればいいのかわからなくなっているのかも
dialogue.English: I might not know what to do anymore.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 1番ショックだったのが、私が資格取得のため勉強しようとしているということをその人に話したときに、「お金がもったいないから、独学で図書館で勉強したほうがいいよ」と、価値観を押し付けられたことですね。
dialogue.English: The most shocking thing was when I told that person I was planning to study for a certification, and they forced their values on me, saying, "That's a waste of money, you should just study on your own at the library."

dialogue.content: その人は約20歳も年上ですが、こんなことを言われるのはビックリしましたね。もうこの人には何も話せないと思いました。
dialogue.English: That person is about 20 years older than me, but I was shocked to be told something like that. I felt I couldn't talk to them about anything anymore.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。新人だと期待と不安の中で頑張ろうとしているのに、邪魔をされた挙句、強制までされるのは心が折れてしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. As a new employee, you're trying your best amidst hope and anxiety, so to be obstructed and have someone's values forced upon you must be spirit-crushing.

dialogue.content: こんな人が1番近い先輩だなんて、誰に頼ればいいのかわかりませんでした。
dialogue.English: With someone like that as my closest senior, I didn't know who I could rely on.

dialogue.content: はい。これも人生経験ですね、、、、笑
dialogue.English: Yes. I guess this is a life experience, too... (laughs)

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。私もさとみさんと似ているか定かではないですが、私も以前の仕事では一つ上の先輩が20以上離れていたので、当時のことを思い出しましまた(笑)
dialogue.English: I see. I'm not sure if our situations are similar, Ms. Satomi, but in my previous job, my immediate senior was also over 20 years older, so this reminds me of that time (laughs).

dialogue.content: 話がなかなか合わなければ、価値観も違うし、何かとタイミングといいますか、合わないことが多かったですね。
dialogue.English: It was hard to find common ground, our values were different, and there were many times when our timing, or something, just didn't align.

dialogue.content: そうなんですか？それだけ歳が離れているという時点で気もつかってしまいますよね、、、、
dialogue.English: Is that so? Just having such a large age gap would make you feel like you have to be extra careful, right?

dialogue.content: そうですね。言葉遣いや態度とか、あとはどう接すればよいかなど、日々色々なことが頭の中を駆け巡っていましたね。
dialogue.English: Yes, it was. I was constantly thinking about things like my choice of words, my attitude, and how best to interact with them.

dialogue.content: ジェネレーションギャップ？？みんなそれぞれ他人なんだし、意見が違うのは当たり前だけど、先輩後輩、同僚という立場なんだから、お互い尊重し合う関係でいたいものですよね
dialogue.English: A generation gap? Everyone is their own person, so it's natural to have different opinions. But as seniors, juniors, and colleagues, you'd hope for a relationship based on mutual respect.

dialogue.content: 接し方は、難しいですよね。馴れ馴れしくするのも失礼かなと思ってしまうし、固くなり過ぎても壁感じるだろうし、、、、
dialogue.English: It's hard to know how to interact. You worry that being too friendly might be rude, but being too formal might create a barrier...

dialogue.content: 仕事のこと以外でも考えることありすぎて、最初は特に神経使いますね、、、、
dialogue.English: There's so much to think about besides the work itself, it's especially nerve-wracking at the beginning...

dialogue.content: そうですよね。意見や価値観が違うのは、20歳も違えば分かりきっていることですから、皆が尊重し合えばいい職場環境になり、仕事のやりたいことややりがいが見つかるかもしれないですものね。
dialogue.English: That's right. It's a given that opinions and values will differ with a 20-year age gap, so if everyone could just respect each other, it would create a better work environment where you might find fulfilling work you want to do.

dialogue.content: こんな事で会社を去るのは、なんだかな～と思ってしまうこともありました。
dialogue.English: There were times I thought it felt a bit strange to be leaving the company over something like this.

dialogue.content: 大変ですよね。私は神経を使いすぎて、初めのころは仕事から帰ったら即ソファにたおれこんでいましたね(笑)
dialogue.English: It is tough. I was so mentally drained that in the beginning, I'd come home from work and collapse straight onto the sofa (laughs).

dialogue.content: やる気、期待があった分心にぽっかりと穴が空いてしまった気持になりますよね。
dialogue.English: When you have so much motivation and hope, it must feel like a huge hole has been left in your heart.

dialogue.content: それは相当でしたね、、、、。
dialogue.English: That sounds like it was quite intense...

dialogue.content: 精神的なものもいつの間にか体にどっしり感じますよね
dialogue.English: The mental strain starts to take a physical toll on you before you even realize it, doesn't it?

dialogue.content: やる気、期待はすごく高かったと思いますね、、、、
dialogue.English: I think my motivation and expectations were really high...

dialogue.content: わたしは寝ても寝ても寝足りなくて、熟睡できていなかったことに、気が付きました。
dialogue.English: I realized that no matter how much I slept, it was never enough—I wasn’t sleeping deeply.

dialogue.content: うんうん。寝れていないと余計に気分が落ち込みますよね。気が付いた後は、寝れるように何か取り組まれたのですか？
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm. Not being able to sleep can make you feel even more down, can't it? After you realized that, did you try anything to help you sleep better?

dialogue.content: はい。昼間も眠くてしんどかったです。
dialogue.English: Yes. I was sleepy and exhausted during the day, too.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。
dialogue.English: I can imagine.

dialogue.content: 漢方とか紅茶を飲むようにしました
dialogue.English: I started drinking things like herbal remedies and tea.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。寝る前に紅茶などを飲むのはリラックスできますものね。飲んだりした際は眠れましたか？
dialogue.English: I see. Drinking something like tea before bed can be very relaxing. Were you able to sleep better when you did that?

dialogue.content: 少し眠れるようになりましたね。
dialogue.English: I started to sleep a little better.

dialogue.content: あとストレッチとか！
dialogue.English: And stretching, too!

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.content: 緊張をほぐすのは大事ですね。
dialogue.English: It's important to relieve tension.

dialogue.content: 相談員さんは何かストレス解消でやってることってありますか？
dialogue.English: Do you do anything to relieve stress, counselor?

dialogue.content: すごく大事ですね。私は、長めにお風呂に入るようにしていますね。あと、最近はリラックスできるアロマを焚いたりもしていますね。（すみません、時間を過ぎましたが続けても大丈夫なのでしょうか？今日が初めてなので、そのあたりがわからなもので）
dialogue.English: It's very important. I try to take long baths. And recently, I've also been using relaxing aromatherapy. (Excuse me, we've gone over our time. Is it alright to continue? This is my first time, so I'm not quite sure of the procedure.)

dialogue.content: お風呂も気持ちいいですね。今日入ってみようかな。アロマもいいですね。
dialogue.English: Baths feel nice, too. Maybe I'll take one today. Aromatherapy sounds good as well.

dialogue.content: あ！時間過ぎてましたね。
dialogue.English: Oh! You're right, we are over time.

dialogue.content: 一応1時間なので、これで終了にしましょうか！
dialogue.English: It’s supposed to be an hour, so shall we wrap up here?

dialogue.content: わかりました！
dialogue.English: Understood!

dialogue.content: いろいろお話聞いていただきありがとうございました！
dialogue.English: Thank you so much for listening to me today!

dialogue.content: 今日はありがとうございました！なかなか上手くいかないものですね(-_-;)いえいえ！こちらこそありがとうございました！またロープレをやる時があればよろしくお願いいたします！では終了しますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you for today! It's harder than it looks, isn't it? (-_-;) Not at all! Thank you as well! I look forward to role-playing with you again if we have the chance! I'll end the session now.

dialogue.content: いえいえ！とてもよかったです。(わたしもまだ初心者ですが)こちらこそよろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Not at all! You were very good. (Though I'm still a beginner myself.) I look forward to working with you again, too.

dialogue.content: では失礼しますね。
dialogue.English: Alright then, take care.
